text:
Introduction

Tuberculosis killed an estimated 1.5 million people in 2020, and drug-resistant strains now account for a growing share of new cases in several high-burden countries. Current regimens last at least six months, and adherence drops sharply after the intensive phase. We screened 1,200 compounds from an open-access library against Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv in a resazurin microtitre assay, and followed up 38 hits with dose-response curves and cytotoxicity in HepG2 cells. Eleven compounds had MIC90 values below 5 uM and selectivity indices above 10. Two of them share a nitroimidazole scaffold that had not been reported against mycobacteria before; the others fall into known chemotypes. We discuss why the hit rate was lower than in earlier screens of the same library, which used a different medium, and we release all raw plate reads so that others can re-analyse them.

Methods

Compounds were dissolved in DMSO at 10 mM and stored at -20 C. Plates were read after seven days of incubation at 37 C.
